statement_blocker: The repository does not select a BCH construction/existence theorem, the BCH designed-distance bound, an actual minimum-distance result, a dimension/redundancy bound, or a decoder-correctness theorem. conclusion: Open: the repository does not say whether to prove construction/existence, the BCH designed-distance lower bound, correction capability derived from distance, a dimension bound, or decoding correctness.

the BCH bound that consecutive roots imply minimum Hamming distance at least a designed distance delta
a correction consequence for up to floor((delta - 1) / 2) errors under a specified decoding notion
a primitive narrow-sense BCH specialization of length q^m - 1 with first root exponent one
a binary primitive t-error-correcting BCH construction with length 2^m - 1 and designed distance 2t + 1
a dimension or redundancy estimate for a BCH code
an algebraic decoding algorithm and its correctness theorem
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: field cardinality zero or one versus the finite-field prime-power constraint
extension degree zero, length zero or one, and length not equal to or not dividing q^m - 1
designed distance zero, one, two, larger than the length, and correction radius zero
primitive versus nonprimitive and narrow-sense versus non-narrow-sense codes
root intervals that wrap modulo the multiplicative order, contain duplicates, or meet characteristic-sensitive cases
zero or unit generator polynomial, the zero/full code, empty root set, and dimension zero or full length
actual versus designed minimum distance, unique versus bounded-distance decoding, received-word ties, and more errors than the stated radius
excluded_substitutions: a definition of a BCH, cyclic, or linear code presented as the requested error-correction theorem
the generic fact that minimum distance at least 2t + 1 permits t-error correction used without a BCH construction and checked bridge
a primitive binary special case presented as a general q-ary or nonprimitive theorem
a designed-distance assertion presented as equality with actual minimum distance
a dimension bound, cyclicity fact, polynomial-root identity, or decoder example presented as the catalog root
a hand-picked finite code, exhaustive test, simulation, or numerical decoder run presented as a universal theorem
the Stage0-only THM-C-0382 record or neighboring code targets used as accepted evidence or to broaden this target
